description: Use when someone asks about a number Tickerz counts: what people do (sports betting in New York, people in New York City shelters, evictions, debt collection complaints, gun background checks, overdose deaths, loneliness), the planet and the net (Arctic sea ice, earthquakes, accounts in breaches), power (executive orders signed), markets (memecoins launched on pump.fun, prediction market volume, jobless claims, people screened at US airports), or the US jobs number, unemployment rate, CPI and core CPI as first published, before the Bureau of Labor Statistics revised them. For a plain question, find_index picks the index. Each index is read against its own normal and each reading is timestamped in Bitcoin so it cannot be changed afterward. Every index: what it counts, its family, its source, the newest period, its score against its own normal (0 to 100) and signed z for the newest complete period, and the last 30 complete periods as period, value and band. For a finished period read latest_complete. latest is the newest period on file; when it has provisional true it is a period still counting, and its change_pct compares it with a full one. Some sources land weeks late, so latest_complete can be behind today. Same data as GET /api/indices. A source whose terms keep its levels out of the API is served with its score and bands only.
name: list_indices
title: Indexes
